# Modern Investing Techniques
💰 **Modern Investing Techniques** — AI-Powered Daily Market Intelligence
> **Trump's call for US rates at 1% or less could force BoC divergence, giving TFSA holders a chance to secure higher yields before any policy shift.**

**Market Pulse:** S&P 500 closed at 7,552 (-0.4%), NASDAQ at 25,978 (flat), and TSX Composite at 35,491 (-0.3%). The Fed raised rates yesterday with Chair Warsh signaling further tightening ahead due to geopolitics and energy shocks. Bank of Canada released its September 2 deliberations summary today, highlighting concerns over US tariffs weighing on confidence. About 21 days ago we picked PNG.V on earnings momentum and it closed down 5.59%, underscoring how quickly project catalysts can fade without volume support. Energy faces fresh pressure after Saudi Arabia cut shipments to Europe following drone attacks, while US home listings hit a four-year high, handing buyers more leverage.
---
### Strategy Spotlight
Holding cash in a TFSA looks safe on paper but quietly loses purchasing power when inflation outpaces the low yields on savings. Today's environment of sticky inflation and shifting rate expectations makes this risk concrete for Canadian investors who default to cash after market volatility. The approach is to run a simple inflation-adjusted return screen on any cash allocation above 20% of the TFSA, comparing it against short-term bond ETFs or dividend payers with growing payouts. Platforms like Wealthsimple or Questrade let you set automatic sweeps from cash into a low-cost bond ladder or covered-call ETF once the real yield turns negative. This strategy performed best in the 2022-2023 period when cash returns lagged CPI by more than 4 percentage points annually. The main risk is opportunity cost if rates rise faster than expected, so cap the shift at 10% of the TFSA per quarter. Investors can start by exporting their current cash balance from the brokerage dashboard and subtracting the most recent twelve-month CPI figure to arrive at a real yield number. If that figure sits below zero, the next step is selecting a short-duration bond ETF with a management fee under 0.20 percent and placing a limit order during the first hour of trading. The same screen can be rerun quarterly to keep the allocation aligned with changing rate paths from both the Bank of Canada and the Federal Reserve. Source: [fool.ca](https://www.fool.ca/2026/09/16/cash-feels-safe-but-this-is-the-tfsa-risk-investors-arent-pricing-in/)
---
### Investor Education: How TFSA Contribution Room Actually Works
Imagine you opened a TFSA in January 2023 with $6,500 in unused room and contributed the full amount on February 1. Your order filled, but the actual room calculation resets every January 1 based on the prior year's unused balance plus the new annual limit, not on the date you clicked buy. Most retail investors don't realize that over-contributing by even $100 triggers a 1% per month penalty on the excess until corrected. The pro tip is to log into your CRA My Account before each contribution and export the exact available room figure rather than relying on your broker's estimate. The common misconception is treating the TFSA like an RRSP where contribution room is lost forever if unused; the fix is to treat every January 1 as a fresh planning checkpoint and set a calendar reminder to check the CRA balance before moving money. The CRA system also carries forward unused room from earlier years without limit, which means a contributor who skipped 2024 can still use that room in 2026 alongside the new annual allotment. Checking the official figure prevents the common error of double-counting room that a brokerage app has already estimated incorrectly after a recent withdrawal. Setting the reminder for the first business day of each year creates a repeatable habit that keeps contribution decisions aligned with the actual CRA ledger rather than an approximation.

**Why This Teaches:** This setup demonstrates waiting for volume confirmation before entering a macro-driven name, directly applying the rule that requires volume above the 20-day average on catalyst trades. Listeners see how to size a position only after the market validates the spending story with actual order flow. The approach also illustrates the value of naming a precise invalidation level tied to a company-specific metric rather than a generic price stop. By monitoring backlog growth instead of headline news flow, the process keeps the thesis anchored to measurable contract momentum. These two ETFs combine S&P 500 and Nasdaq-100 exposure with a covered-call overlay that generates monthly income while retaining upside to the strike. Canadian investors gain an edge by collecting premium in a TFSA without US withholding tax complications on the option portion. The funds crossed 3 trillion won in assets this week, showing strong retail adoption. Access them through any Canadian brokerage that offers Mirae Asset products; the covered-call structure is listed under the TIGER family. The monthly distribution schedule aligns with TFSA contribution timing, allowing investors to reinvest premiums automatically inside the account without triggering taxable events. Because the call overlay caps upside only above the strike, the structure still participates in moderate equity gains while providing a buffer during flat or slightly down periods. Source: [asiae.co.kr](https://www.asiae.co.kr/en/article/stock-etc/2026091709110389213)

**Saudi Arabia cuts oil shipments to Europe after drone attacks**
The move tightens supply into a key market and adds upward pressure on global energy prices just as the Fed cited geopolitics as a reason for further hikes. Canadian energy producers with European export exposure could see margin expansion if the supply disruption persists beyond the current quarter. The timing coincides with the Bank of Canada’s own concerns about external shocks, creating a cross-border linkage that affects both oil prices and domestic rate expectations.
**Action:** Trim energy exposure if crude closes above its 20-day high without a corresponding volume spike on Canadian producers.

**U.S. home listings rose 2.6% MoM to highest in over 4 years**
Redfin data shows more supply hitting the market, improving buyer leverage and potentially capping price gains in US housing-related names. The increase in listings reverses a multi-year trend of tight inventory and gives homebuilders more competition for each sale. Investors holding US REITs or homebuilder ETFs can use the higher listing count as an early signal that shelter inflation components in upcoming CPI prints may moderate.
**Action:** Add US homebuilder ETFs to the watchlist only after the next CPI print confirms cooling shelter inflation.

**Dollarama stock wrestles with premium valuation after strong Q2**
The retailer beat expectations yet trades at elevated multiples, creating a classic valuation test case for Canadian consumer discretionary names. The post-earnings reaction highlights how quickly multiples can compress when growth slows even modestly. Running a forward P/E comparison against sector peers provides a concrete way to decide whether the current price already prices in the strong quarter.
**Action:** Run a 12-month forward P/E screen on DOL.TO and compare it to the TSX consumer sector average before adding.

**Power One receives drill permit for Pecors project**
The permit clears the way for deeper testing of a magnetic anomaly near Elliot Lake, giving a small-cap exploration name a concrete catalyst. The project sits approximately 14 kilometres east of Elliot Lake, Ontario, and the permit allows diamond drilling to begin once surface work is complete. Speculative names at this stage require assay confirmation before any position is sized, because drill results can shift the valuation narrative quickly.
**Action:** Place Pecors on the speculative watchlist and wait for assay results before any position sizing.

This podcast is for EDUCATIONAL and ENTERTAINMENT purposes only. Nothing discussed constitutes financial advice, investment recommendations, or solicitations to buy or sell securities. The "Practice Investment of the Day" uses SIMULATED trades with NO real money — it is a learning exercise to demonstrate analytical techniques. Past performance does not predict future results. **Market Pulse:** S&P 500 closed at 7,586 (-0.4%), NASDAQ Composite at 25,982 (-0.8%), and TSX Composite at 35,582 (-0.3%). Markets are pricing a 94% chance of a Fed rate hike this week with futures also pointing to a second move before year-end. Breadth improved sharply Monday with 53 S&P names beating the index versus 74 lagging, narrowing the net breadth deficit from -85 to -21. About 20 days ago we picked PNG.V which closed -5.59%; earnings momentum faded without volume support. The nearest central-bank decision sits with the Federal Reserve this week, where futures now embed not only the initial hike but a follow-on move by December. Earnings season has largely cleared for most large-cap names, leaving sector rotation and rate-sensitive leadership as the dominant weekly drivers. Healthcare flipped from the weakest sector to positive in a single session, illustrating how quickly capital can reallocate even on a down day for the headline index.
---
### Strategy Spotlight
Breadth readings act as an early filter for whether a market move has participation or is just a narrow handful of names carrying the index. Today's flip from negative to less-negative breadth on a down day for the S&P shows how sector rotation can produce quick reversals in leadership even when headline indices finish lower. The S&P itself fell 0.48 percent, yet the number of stocks beating the index rose from 30 on Friday to 53 on Monday while laggards fell from 115 to 74, moving net breadth from -85 to -21. Investors can track this by comparing the number of stocks above their 20-day average to those below it, or by watching the advance-decline line on the same platform that supplies their charts. The approach works best when a single session's breadth swing exceeds recent averages, as it did Monday, because that signals capital is rotating rather than exiting. Risk appears when breadth improves but volume stays below the 20-day average, leaving the move vulnerable to quick reversal. Platforms such as TradingView or Thinkorswim let users overlay breadth indicators directly on index charts for daily checks. Canadian investors can apply the same filter inside a TFSA by screening TSX names for the same advance-decline differential before committing new capital. Source: [x.com](https://x.com/OptionsPlay/status/2099849466345881641)

### Investor Education: Naming Your Invalidation Before You Buy
Imagine you bought a data-centre name last week after it posted record quarterly sales and raised guidance. Your order filled at the open, yet the position is already down 4% because the broader tech rotation you assumed would support it never arrived. The mechanism is simple: without a written invalidation, every dip gets rationalized as noise until the loss grows large enough to force an exit that hindsight then labels a mistake. Professionals write the exact observable trigger first—such as “if the next two sessions close below the 50-day moving average on volume above the 20-day average, the rotation thesis is dead”—then set the stop at that level. Most retail investors skip this step and later describe the loss only as “it went down,” which prevents learning what actually broke. The concrete fix is to type the invalidation sentence into the same note where you record the entry thesis before the order is placed. This practice converts a loss from an emotional event into a data point about which assumption failed. It also forces the investor to define success and failure in observable market terms rather than in feelings about the name. Over repeated trades the habit reveals patterns in which types of invalidation trigger most often, allowing the investor to refine entry criteria before the next position is sized.

The cold-streak regime check advises raising the bar for any new entry, which is why the position remains on watch rather than deployed. Sector concentration rules also require avoiding the “other” category that has dominated recent trades.
- **Target:** +4% to +8% over five sessions if volume confirms and sector rotation holds. The target range assumes the valuation narrative draws incremental buyers once volume clears the 20-day average.
- **Confidence Level:** Medium — the valuation narrative is confirmed by the analyst comment, yet sector rotation signals remain mixed and volume confirmation is still pending. The medium rating reflects two aligned factors (narrative catalyst plus price above the 50-day average) offset by the pending volume gate and the broader regime caution.

**Why This Teaches:** The setup forces an explicit volume gate before entry, directly applying the rule that catalyst names already in rotation require volume above the 20-day average. It also demonstrates how to keep a name on a watchlist during a cold streak without forcing capital deployment. The approach separates narrative excitement from tradable confirmation, a distinction that becomes more valuable when multiple desks are revising forecasts simultaneously. The scanner surfaces large options trades in real time with filters for size, unusual activity, and underlying sector. The scanner also tags trades by size and premium, allowing users to distinguish between small speculative bets and large institutional blocks. Canadian users can apply the same filters to U.S.-listed names that frequently appear in cross-listed Canadian portfolios. Source: [x.com](https://x.com/unusual_whales/status/2100099384839115180)
---

**High Tide turns profitable on record sales**
The Canadian cannabis retailer posted its first profitable quarter alongside all-time high revenue, showing operating leverage after years of cost cuts. The result demonstrates that scale and margin discipline can coexist even in a heavily regulated domestic market. 
**Action:** Add HITI.V to the TFSA watchlist and review the next earnings release for margin sustainability.

Early discussions with investors could value the company above $1.2 trillion and set a new benchmark for private AI valuations. The round would exceed any prior private technology financing and could influence how public AI-infrastructure suppliers are priced. 
**Action:** Watch for any listed AI-infrastructure suppliers that disclose direct exposure to OpenAI contracts.

Investors who skip the fee audit often discover that high-cost ETFs have quietly eroded 40-60 basis points of annual return over multiple quarters. Earnings reports from growth names like robotics and mining developers offer a repeatable way to capture short-term alpha when results beat expectations on both revenue and project milestones. Screen for companies that pair positive earnings with concrete project catalysts such as equipment financing LOIs or lifted suspensions, then enter only if volume exceeds the 20-day average on the reaction day. Risk comes from low-float names that gap and reverse on thin volume, so always set a hard stop at the pre-report low. Source: [bnnbloomberg.ca](https://www.bnnbloomberg.ca/press-releases/2026/08/27/kraken-robotics-reports-q2-2026-financial-results/)

### Investor Education: Reading Between the Lines of Earnings Releases
Imagine you bought shares in a TSX-V mining name the morning after it reported Q2 results and a new equipment financing LOI. Your order filled at the open, yet the stock faded by midday. What actually happened is that the headline numbers looked strong but the LOI was non-binding, so institutions that had pre-positioned sold into the retail rush. The mechanism is simple: reported revenue or project progress moves the stock only when accompanied by binding cash flow visibility, otherwise the initial pop is absorbed by earlier buyers locking in gains. Most retail investors skip the fine print on whether the catalyst is binding or aspirational and end up holding the bag after the first-hour volume spike. The pro tip is to open the full MD&A within 30 minutes of the release and check for words like “non-binding” or “subject to final documentation” before adding to size. The concrete misconception to avoid is treating every positive headline as equal; the fix is to require at least one line item that converts directly into near-term cash or production before treating the reaction as confirmed. Troilus Mining Corp. announced a non-binding Letter of Interest from Finnvera plc for up to approximately US$132 million in potential export credit support tied to Metso equipment procurement for its Québec gold-copper project. The press release explicitly labels the LOI as non-binding, which means any price reaction must be discounted until further documentation converts the support into a firm commitment. Patagonia Gold Corp. reported that a preventive, partial and temporary suspension at its Calcatreu Project in Argentina was lifted after an agreement with the Secretariat of Labour of the Province of Rio Negro on hiring and training local workers. That development carries more immediate operational weight because the suspension itself has been removed rather than merely proposed. Blossom Gold Inc. released initial bottle roll test results from multiple host rock types at its Rosebud Open-Pit Heap-Leach Project in Nevada, with Kappes, Cassiday and Associates conducting the program. Those test parameters appear in the release and can be reviewed line-by-line to assess recovery consistency across oxidized and fresh rock before any valuation adjustment. Astra Exploration Inc. qualified to trade on the OTCQX Best Market after upgrading from the OTCQB Venture Market, a step that improves U.S. investor access without requiring a full NYSE listing.
